A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same boosting study. All 43 pages of each version, including Appendices A–D, are readable; text extraction and rendered-page comparisons support reliable matching of equations, tables, figures, and relocated passages.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments across 20 binary-classification datasets, including accuracy, sparsity, runtime, margin, reweighting, and optimal-tree results in the main text and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical study and reports revised optimal-tree results in Section 7 and Appendix D.7.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the NM-Boost and QRLP-Boost formulations, and the described learner procedures are unchanged. Replaced optimal-tree scores do not establish an algorithmic modification.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 20 binary-classification datasets and retain the CART, confidence-rated voting, reweighting, and optimal-tree scenarios. Appendix A's dataset descriptions merely shift across pages.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged. The optimal-tree comparisons retain six totally corrective methods and Adaboost; the main CART benchmarks continue to include XGBoost and LightGBM.

E3.justification: The stated splits, preprocessing, hyperparameter sweeps, tree depths, accuracy/sparsity metrics, 100-iteration limit, and 45-minute budget are unchanged. Figure 17 aggregates retained settings. No protocol revision explaining the replaced optimal-tree results is documented.

E4.justification: Appendix D.7 adds an explicit joint accuracy–sparsity comparison between ODT and CART ensembles through Figure 17. Previously, optimal-tree accuracy and column counts appeared in tables without this direct trade-off comparison. Other analysis families remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over five seeds, standard-deviation error bars, and the same statistical reporting practices. Changed deviations and statements about significant differences accompany revised results, without a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Optimal-tree results are extensively replaced in Tables 17–20 and Figures 10–11. For example, Table 17 changes NM-Boost's depth-1 mean accuracy from 0.750 to 0.805 and mean active columns from 6.3 to 23.2. Reported ODT inferiority becomes approximate parity with CART under unchanged stated settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, optimization formulations, constraints, and theoretical reasoning in Sections 2–4 and Appendix B are unchanged. No proof, formal assumption, or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: Section 8 replaces the conclusion that optimal trees often reduce performance, particularly for totally corrective methods, with the claim that performance is often similar to CART and may improve depending on the dataset. This substantially revises a principal empirical conclusion, although the abstract and contribution list remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 7 removes the Adaboost-specific explanation that stage-wise training protects diversity while totally corrective reweighting exacerbates similarity. Reduced diversity becomes a tentative explanation for limited improvement rather than general degradation. v3 also concludes that ODTs have no consistent sparsity advantage or disadvantage.

D1.justification: Implementation libraries, software versions, hardware, hyperparameters, preprocessing instructions, and code/data access disclosures are unchanged. No technical explanation for the extensive optimal-tree result replacements is supplied.

R1.justification: The reference list and related-work survey are unchanged. Both versions position the work as a broad empirical study extending earlier LP-based boosting research and Aglin et al.'s smaller optimal-tree study.

P1.justification: Section 7 and the optimal-tree passage in Section 8 are locally rewritten and shortened, with small additions in Appendix D.7. The overall section organization, abstract, introduction, and remaining narrative are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 10–11 are redrawn with revised vertical scales, and Appendix D.7 gains the four-panel Figure 17. Local text and table layout shifts accompany these changes; the overall visual design and remaining displays are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the ODT–CART sparsity comparison easier to inspect and reduces speculative mechanism explanations. However, the extensive replacement of Tables 17–20 reverses an important conclusion without explaining a correction or procedural change. The PDFs establish presentation benefits but leave the reliability of the dominant empirical revision unresolved, preventing a confident overall quality judgment.
